work.title: Two Android apps, shipped end to end.
work.intro: I designed, directed and shipped both. I’m a web developer, so I built them through an AI-directed workflow — not hand-coded React Native — and I say so up front.

projects.name: Dawa2
projects.desc: A private, offline medication reminder for Android. Real full-screen alarms keep ringing until you answer Taken, Snooze or Skip. English and Arabic. No accounts, no cloud.
projects.how: AI-directed: I wrote the spec, chose the UI from mockups, steered Claude Code through the plan, and tested every alarm on my own phone.

projects.name: Fakkerni
projects.desc: An Arabic-first alarm and reminder app. Reminders that ring offline, medication with dose tracking and refills, and encrypted backups to Google Drive. Right-to-left throughout.
projects.how: Same workflow: spec, mockups, Claude Code, real-device testing. I chose every feature and decided what shipped.

ai.title: How I work with AI
ai.lead: A deliberate workflow, not autocomplete. I own the product decisions; AI implements what I direct, and I review and test it.

steps.d: Shape the idea and write the spec with ChatGPT.
Compare Claude Design mockups and choose a direction.
Steer Claude Code through the implementation plan, milestone by milestone.
Run it on the emulator and on my own phone.
Choose the features, cut the rest, own the release.

ai.note: Dawa2 and Fakkerni were built this way. I didn’t hand-write their React Native or Kotlin — my hands-on stack is Laravel and Next.js.
